pass_b_english: The altars will be reduced to fine dust, and the trees will not remain, for their idols will be cut down like a forest.
The prophet, having rebuked those who have acted impiously against the holy prophets, now speaks as if from the face of God, saying that the iniquity of Jacob will be removed.

This removal of iniquity is not like human judgment, for God's judgment is tempered with gentleness, and He overcomes human weaknesses, always conquering human petty-mindedness, and not always exacting punishment for earthly transgressions in equal measure.

The blessing promised to Abraham is the forgiveness of sins, which is the way of the blessing for those who have not done good, but have been forgiven, as God said to Abraham, 'I will bless you and multiply your seed' (Genesis 22:17).

If God had not blessed Abraham with the forgiveness of sins, his seed would not have been multiplied, for they would have been punished for their sins, but instead, the hypothesis of the blessing has been kept and passed to them, and they have received forgiveness.

The time will come when the faithful will be free from their transgressions, and this will happen when they wage war against the ancient error that has held them captive, and when altars and temples and the smoke of idols will be removed, and the temples built for lifeless idols will be consumed by fire.
As they cut down the trees and handmade objects that were once revered, they will be like a grove being cleared, and God will raise up those who have stumbled from Israel.
This is in line with the divine Paul's statement that when the fullness of the nations enters, then all Israel will be saved (Romans 11:25).

The complete destruction of temples, the removal of groves, and the addition of the destruction of statues will signify a change from the ancient error to the knowledge of truth, and the people will turn to the truth, abandoning their former idols and the works of their own hands.
